notes.text: Erik Gustafsson is day to day and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Brian Dumoulin has taken his spot beside Brandt Clarke.
Kevin Fiala returned in their last game after missing 16 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Easton Cowan has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 47:37 together, down from 72% with Marchenko.

Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 59:20 together, up from 48% with Blankenburg.
Morgan Rielly is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Oliver Ekman-Larsson has taken his spot beside Troy Stecher.
Ryan Tverberg was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside John Tavares and William Nylander.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 21 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Kings go in seventh in the Pacific with 12 points, the Maple Leafs seventh in the Atlantic with 18 points.

TOR.head: Not an easy night for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage and gets Tanev back, Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs’ best way through is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: The Maple Leafs need a win
paras: The Maple Leafs are on a five-game losing streak, and the Kings are on a three-game losing streak. Going in, the Kings are seventh in the Pacific (30th in the NHL) and the Leafs seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 23rd).

The Kings have played better than their record (.353) says: their chances are worth about .629, and their finishing has held them back. The Maple Leafs’ record (.429) is about what their chances are worth.

The Maple Leafs (31st) and the Kings (30th) both have had shaky goaltending. The Kings leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest) and keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (2nd). On the other side, the Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). The Kings are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs. Beyond that, the Kings hound the puck, but the Maple Leafs sit back.

Artemi Panarin (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 17 GP) is carrying the Kings’ offense. Auston Matthews (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 21 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is sixth in the NHL, and William Nylander (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind.

Darcy Kuemper (5-5-1 / .873 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for Los Angeles. Toronto has two options in net: Sergei Bobrovsky (3-8-2 / .881 SV% in 13 GS) and Anthony Stolarz (5-3-0 / .900 SV% in 8 GS). Bobrovsky has started six of their last ten games, but Stolarz got the last one on Nov 12. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
